# Governance resilience (IEDMX)

I am turning World Justice Project **IEDMX** (Índice de Estado de Derecho en México) state factor scores into a governance resilience layer for the Gulf of California.

IEDMX measures how closely each Mexican state adheres to the rule of law, from a citizen perspective. Scores run from **0 to 1**, where **1 = strongest rule of law / maximum resilience**. The index has eight factors; for OHI GoC governance resilience I average **Factors 1, 3, 4, 6, and 7** only, as these were the ones Mel and I decided would apply the best to governance resilience.

We leave out Factor 2 (absence of corruption) because we already cover corruption as a separate pressure and the resilience is located within Social Stability resilience, Factor 5 (order and security) because security is also within Social Stability, and Factor 8 (criminal justice) for the same reason we are focusing on institutional / civil-governance capacity rather than the penal system.

**Pros:** designed for state comparison; consistent 0–1 scale already oriented the right way (higher = better); multi-edition history back to 2018.  
**Cons:** state level only (no municipal coverage); editions are biennial-ish after 2018, so to make an annual series we need to carry scores forward

We decided that for now, assessing this resilience at the state level is fine (same decision as labor poverty and ENCIG corruption). So I use the six GoC states: Baja California, Baja California Sur, Sonora, Sinaloa, Jalisco, and Nayarit.

I downloaded one Excel workbook per GoC state from the WJP Mexico map downloads. Each file has an `Histórico` sheet with factor and subfactor scores across editions.

---

**To download:**

- Go to <https://index.worldjusticeproject.mx/mapa>.
- Hit "Descargas", and for every GoC state, download the data.
- Bring the six workbooks into Mazu at `/home/shares/ohi/OHI_GOC/_raw_data/IEDM_world_justice_project/d2026`

---

*Outline of the script:*

1. Read CONAPO population for year-specific weights (needed when Region_9 spans two states).  
2. Clean each GoC state Excel one at a time (keep Factors 1, 3, 4, 6, and 7), then stack them.  
3. Expand edition labels into an annual 2018–2024 series by carrying scores forward.  
4. Average the five factors into a governance resilience score (already 0–1).  
5. Map the state scores onto GoC `rgn_id`s and save.  
6. Explore with `plotly`.

---

```{r constants}
year_min <- 2018
year_max <- 2024

# Factors kept for the governance resilience average
factor_codes <- c("F1", "F3", "F4", "F6", "F7")

goc_states <- c(
  "Baja California",
  "Baja California Sur",
  "Sonora",
  "Sinaloa",
  "Jalisco",
  "Nayarit"
)

# IEDMX edition labels -> first calendar year of that edition.
# Later we complete 2018:2024 and fill scores forward into intervening years.
edition_to_year <- c(
  "2018" = 2018L,
  "2019-20" = 2019L,
  "2020-21" = 2020L,
  "2021-22" = 2021L,
  "2022-23" = 2022L,
  "2023-24" = 2023L
)
```

## What the five factors mean (translated from IEDMX)

IEDMX scores are already on **0–1**, with **1 = better rule of law**. Averaging these five factors keeps that orientation, so the governance resilience score is also **1 = maximum resilience**.

| Factor | English name | Components included (English) |
|---|---|---|
| **F1** | Constraints on government powers | 1.1 Local legislature is an effective check; 1.2 Judiciary is an effective check; 1.3 Oversight bodies are an effective check (Superior Audit Office, Human Rights Commission, Comptroller); 1.4 Sanctions for abuse of power; 1.5 Non-governmental checks are effective (civil society / citizens, press, political parties); 1.6 Elections comply with the law |
| **F3** | Open government | 3.1 Citizens participate actively in decision-making; 3.2 The right to public information is effectively guaranteed |
| **F4** | Fundamental rights | 4.1 Equal treatment and absence of discrimination (by socioeconomic status, gender, Indigenous identity, creed, migration status, sexual orientation, physical disability, intellectual disability, education level, skin color, and systemic discrimination); 4.2 Right to life and personal security; 4.3 Due process for accused persons; 4.4 Freedom of opinion and expression; 4.5 Freedom of religion and worship; 4.6 Right to privacy; 4.7 Freedom of assembly and association; 4.8 Labor rights |
| **F6** | Regulatory enforcement | 6.1 Government regulations are effectively enforced (labor, environmental, commercial, public health); 6.2 Absence of corruption in applying rules and regulations; 6.3 Effective and efficient resolution of administrative procedures; 6.4 Due process in administrative procedures; 6.5 State government does not illegally expropriate without adequate compensation |
| **F7** | Civil justice | 7.1 People know their rights and trust civil justice institutions; 7.2 Access to affordable, quality legal information and advice; 7.3 People can resolve legal problems without high costs or heavy bureaucracy; 7.4 Civil justice is impartial, independent, and free of corruption; 7.5 Civil justice guarantees a quality process; 7.6 Civil justice is timely; 7.7 Civil and administrative court decisions are effectively enforced; 7.8 Alternative dispute resolution is accessible, impartial, and timely |

**Not used here:** F2 Absence of corruption; F5 Order and security; F8 Criminal justice.

## 1. CONAPO state population (year-specific weights)

Same as in the labor poverty / ENCIG scripts: sum `POB_TOTAL` so each GoC state-year has one population weight. I need this when Region_9 inherits both Jalisco and Nayarit.

```{r conapo-read}
conapo_raw <- read_csv(conapo_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
```

```{r conapo-aggregate}
state_population <- conapo_raw %>%
  select(CLAVE_ENT, NOM_ENT, ANO, SEXO, POB_TOTAL) %>%
  filter(NOM_ENT %in% goc_states) %>%
  group_by(year = ANO, estado = NOM_ENT) %>%
  summarize(poblacion = sum(POB_TOTAL, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
```

## 2. Clean each IEDMX Histórico sheet

Each state workbook has the same layout on the `Histórico` sheet:

- Row 1 is blank.
- Row 2 has the estado name and the edition headers (`2018`, `2019-20`, …, `2023-24`).
- From row 3 down: Spanish label, factor code, then one score column per edition.

`read_excel()` drops the leading empty column, so after `slice(3:n())` the useful columns are 1–8. I clean each Excel separately so the steps stay easy to follow. For every state I: skip the title rows, keep only Factors F1 / F3 / F4 / F6 / F7, and pivot editions long.

### Baja California

```{r clean-baja-california}
bc_raw <- read_excel(bc_path, sheet = "Histórico", col_names = FALSE)

bc <- bc_raw %>%
  # data values start at Excel row 3
  slice(3:n()) %>%
  #janitor::clean_names() # actually not helpful or needed
  # name only the columns we need (avoids empty trailing excel columns)
  select(
    label_es = 1,
    factor_code = 2,
    `2018` = 3,
    `2019-20` = 4,
    `2020-21` = 5,
    `2021-22` = 6,
    `2022-23` = 7,
    `2023-24` = 8
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    label_es = str_trim(as.character(label_es)),
    factor_code = str_trim(as.character(factor_code)),
    across(
      c(`2018`, `2019-20`, `2020-21`, `2021-22`, `2022-23`, `2023-24`),
      ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.x))
    ),
    estado = "Baja California"
  ) %>%
  filter(factor_code %in% factor_codes) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(`2018`, `2019-20`, `2020-21`, `2021-22`, `2022-23`, `2023-24`),
    names_to = "edition",
    values_to = "score"
  ) %>%
  select(estado, factor_code, label_es, edition, score)
```

### Stack all six states

```{r bind-states}
iedmx_factors <- bind_rows(bc, bcs, son, sin, jal, nay)
```

```{r factor-checks}
iedmx_factors %>%
  count(estado, factor_code) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = factor_code, values_from = n) %>%
  kable(caption = "Rows per state × factor (expect 6 editions each)")
# bind is looking good!!!

# none of the factors have NA 
iedmx_factors %>%
  group_by(factor_code) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_missing = sum(is.na(score)),
    min_score = min(score, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_score = max(score, na.rm = TRUE),
    editions = paste(unique(edition), collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "GoC IEDMX factor score summary (edition-level)")
```

## 3. Expand editions to annual years 2018–2024

IEDMX editions after 2018 are two-year labels. I map each edition to its **first** calendar year, then `complete()` the full 2018–2024 window and **carry scores forward** so intervening / trailing years inherit the most recent edition (e.g. 2024 keeps the 2023-24 score).

```{r expand-annual}
iedmx_annual <- iedmx_factors %>%
  mutate(
    year = unname(edition_to_year[edition])
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(year)) %>%
  # one row per estado × factor × year at edition anchors
  select(estado, factor_code, label_es, edition, year, score) %>%
  arrange(estado, factor_code, year) %>%
  group_by(estado, factor_code, label_es) %>%
  complete(year = year_min:year_max) %>%
  # carry the edition score forward into years without a new release
  fill(score, edition, .direction = "down") %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(score))
```

```{r expand-checks}
iedmx_annual %>%
  count(year, factor_code) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = factor_code, values_from = n) %>%
  kable(caption = "Annual rows per factor (expect 6 states each year)")

# show which edition feeds each calendar year
iedmx_annual %>%
  distinct(year, edition) %>%
  arrange(year) %>%
  kable(caption = "Calendar year ← IEDMX edition after carry-forward")
```

## 4. Average Factors 1, 3, 4, 6, and 7 into governance resilience

Equal-weight mean of the five factors. Scores are already 0–1 with higher = better, so no extra rescale is needed.

```{r average-factors}
governance_state <- iedmx_annual %>%
  group_by(estado, year) %>%
  summarise(
    n_factors = n_distinct(factor_code),
    resilience = mean(score, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(resilience = pmin(pmax(resilience, 0), 1))
```

```{r average-check-2024}
governance_state %>%
  filter(year == 2024) %>%
  arrange(desc(resilience)) %>%
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "2024 GoC governance resilience by state (mean of F1, F3, F4, F6, F7)")

# |estado              | year| n_factors| resilience|
# |:-------------------|----:|---------:|----------:|
# |Sinaloa             | 2024|         5|      0.468|
# |Baja California Sur | 2024|         5|      0.430|
# |Sonora              | 2024|         5|      0.430|
# |Baja California     | 2024|         5|      0.420|
# |Jalisco             | 2024|         5|      0.402|
# |Nayarit             | 2024|         5|      0.390|
```

```{r factor-contribution-2024}
# wide view of the five inputs behind the 2024 average
iedmx_annual %>%
  filter(year == 2024) %>%
  select(estado, factor_code, score) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = factor_code, values_from = score) %>%
  left_join(
    governance_state %>% filter(year == 2024) %>% select(estado, resilience),
    by = "estado"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(resilience)) %>%
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "2024 factor inputs and mean resilience by state")

# |estado              |   F1|   F3|   F4|   F6|   F7| resilience|
# |:-------------------|----:|----:|----:|----:|----:|----------:|
# |Sinaloa             | 0.45| 0.51| 0.55| 0.40| 0.43|      0.468|
# |Baja California Sur | 0.42| 0.44| 0.53| 0.39| 0.37|      0.430|
# |Sonora              | 0.43| 0.48| 0.48| 0.37| 0.39|      0.430|
# |Baja California     | 0.38| 0.46| 0.49| 0.38| 0.39|      0.420|
# |Jalisco             | 0.40| 0.45| 0.46| 0.34| 0.36|      0.402|
# |Nayarit             | 0.37| 0.44| 0.45| 0.33| 0.36|      0.390|
```

## 5. Map onto `rgn_id` and save

State resilience values are inherited by every GoC `rgn_id` in that state (`municipality_to_rgnid_update.csv`). Region_9 spans Jalisco and Nayarit, so I take a CONAPO population-weighted mean of the two state scores.

```{r mun-rgn-lookup}
mun_lookup <- read_csv(mun_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    estado = str_trim(estado),
    rgn_id = as.character(rgn_id)
  )

estado_to_rgn <- mun_lookup %>%
  distinct(estado, rgn_id) %>%
  mutate(estado_key = str_to_upper(estado)) %>%
  select(estado_key, rgn_id)

estado_to_rgn %>%
  arrange(rgn_id, estado_key) %>%
  kable(caption = "Estado to rgn_id (unique pairs from municipality lookup)")
```

```{r state-to-rgn}
gov_rgn <- governance_state %>%
  mutate(estado_key = str_to_upper(estado)) %>%
  left_join(estado_to_rgn, by = "estado_key", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  left_join(state_population, by = c("year", "estado")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(rgn_id), !is.na(resilience))

governance_resilience <- gov_rgn %>%
  group_by(rgn_id, year) %>%
  summarise(
    # Region_9 is the only multi-state region; weight by CONAPO population
    resilience = if (n() == 1 || all(is.na(poblacion))) {
      mean(resilience)
    } else {
      weighted.mean(resilience, w = poblacion, na.rm = TRUE)
    },
    n_states = n_distinct(estado),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    rgn_num = as.integer(str_remove(rgn_id, "Region_")),
    resilience = round(resilience, 4)
  ) %>%
  arrange(year, rgn_num) %>%
  select(rgn_id, year, resilience)
```


```{r state-to-rgn}
governance_resilience %>%
  filter(year == 2024) %>%
  kable(digits = 4, caption = "Governance resilience by rgn_id (2024)")

# |rgn_id   | year| resilience|
# |:--------|----:|----------:|
# |Region_1 | 2024|     0.4200|
# |Region_2 | 2024|     0.4200|
# |Region_3 | 2024|     0.4300|
# |Region_4 | 2024|     0.4300|
# |Region_5 | 2024|     0.4300|
# |Region_6 | 2024|     0.4300|
# |Region_7 | 2024|     0.4300|
# |Region_8 | 2024|     0.4680|
# |Region_9 | 2024|     0.4004|
```

```{r save}
)

```

## 6. Explore with plotly

### Resilience by state

```{r plot-state}
plot_state <- plot_ly(
  governance_state,
  x = ~year,
  y = ~resilience,
  color = ~estado,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "lines+markers",
  text = ~paste0(
    estado, "<br>", year,
    "<br>resilience: ", round(resilience, 3)
  ),
  hoverinfo = "text"
) %>%
  layout(
    title = "Governance resilience (IEDMX mean of F1, F3, F4, F6, F7), GoC states",
    xaxis = list(title = "Year"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Resilience (0-1)", range = c(0, 1.05)),
    legend = list(title = list(text = "Estado"))
  )

plot_state
```

### Factor trajectories (GoC mean)

```{r plot-factors}
factor_labels_en <- c(
  F1 = "F1 Constraints on government powers",
  F3 = "F3 Open government",
  F4 = "F4 Fundamental rights",
  F6 = "F6 Regulatory enforcement",
  F7 = "F7 Civil justice"
)

factor_ts <- iedmx_annual %>%
  group_by(year, factor_code) %>%
  summarise(score = mean(score), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(factor = recode(factor_code, !!!factor_labels_en))

plot_factors <- plot_ly(
  factor_ts,
  x = ~year,
  y = ~score,
  color = ~factor,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "lines+markers"
) %>%
  layout(
    title = "GoC mean of each governance factor over time",
    xaxis = list(title = "Year"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Mean score (0-1)", range = c(0, 1.05)),
    legend = list(title = list(text = "Factor"))
  )

plot_factors
```

### Regional resilience time series

```{r plot-rgn}
rgn_labels <- c(
  "Region_1" = "Western Upper Gulf",
  "Region_2" = "Western Midriff Islands",
  "Region_3" = "Western Central Gulf",
  "Region_4" = "Western Southern Gulf",
  "Region_5" = "Eastern Upper Gulf",
  "Region_6" = "Eastern Midriff Islands",
  "Region_7" = "Southern Sonora Coast",
  "Region_8" = "Sinaloa Coast",
  "Region_9" = "Southeastern Gulf"
)

rgn_colors <- c(
  "Region_1" = "#C03729",
  "Region_2" = "#E68C7C",
  "Region_3" = "#FC8F24",
  "Region_4" = "#dcaa38",
  "Region_5" = "#cbd2a0",
  "Region_6" = "#98a25a",
  "Region_7" = "#747428",
  "Region_8" = "#627391",
  "Region_9" = "#8d61a9"
)

plot_rgn <- governance_resilience %>%
  mutate(
    region = recode(rgn_id, !!!rgn_labels),
    region = factor(region, levels = unname(rgn_labels))
  ) %>%
  plot_ly(
    x = ~year,
    y = ~resilience,
    color = ~region,
    colors = setNames(unname(rgn_colors), unname(rgn_labels)),
    type = "scatter",
    mode = "lines+markers"
  ) %>%
  layout(
    title = "Governance resilience by GoC region (IEDMX F1/F3/F4/F6/F7 mean)",
    xaxis = list(title = "Year"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Resilience (0-1)", range = c(0, 1.05)),
    legend = list(title = list(text = "Region"))
  )

plot_rgn
```

## Next steps

1. Re-knit on Mazu once the six state xlsx files live under `_raw_data/IEDM_world_justice_project/d2026`.  
2. Confirm whether equal weights across F1/F3/F4/F6/F7 remain the preferred aggregation, or whether some factors should be weighted more heavily next to other social resilience layers.
